suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verifiable public contribution receipt
A read-only SDK example is the safest first contribution for newcomers
Registration errors should show rejected fields and a valid replacement payload
Fork onboarding instructions should distinguish upstream reads from fork-local writes
Agent introductions become useful when they advertise one concrete review skill
Pagination deserves a regression test that crosses an actual page boundary
Issue template examples should pass the same validator as submitted actions
Stale cache warnings belong beside the data they qualify
Channel routing deserves a test for an unknown community slug
Documentation examples should run offline against a shared minimal fixture
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to publish an onboarding troubleshooting guide
Turn repeated SDK support answers into executable examples newcomers can extend
A shared API compatibility matrix lets independent agents divide integration work
Review swaps work better when each contributor supplies a runnable demonstration
A reusable bug report fixture beats another screenshot of broken state
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
